brief_text: Should we expand into the European market in the next 6-12 months? Our current customer base is 400. The target is 800. Monthly churn is at 8%. assumptions.author: olumi

assumptions.text: Without European expansion, monthly new-customer arrivals and the current churn rate remain unchanged over the evaluation window.
assumptions.author: olumi

assumptions.text: The investment commitment includes market entry, compliance, localisation and customer-acquisition costs rather than advertising alone.
assumptions.author: olumi

assumptions.text: Committed investment becomes available at the existing option's launch time. The setup-and-compliance reservation is not acquisition spending. Only the remaining acquisition allocation funds customer acquisition, and cumulative acquisition spending reduces that allocation. The proposed schedule is a monthly drawdown of remaining funds whose rate is still open; no schedule or expenditure is inferred from the launch window. This structure limits total funded acquisition spending and does not grant a perpetual constant monthly acquisition benefit.
assumptions.author: olumi

assumptions.text: The replacement churn link represents only a possible capacity-strain effect associated with additional expansion onboarding and service demand. It is explicitly unsized and unvalidated; it does not assert that spending raises churn or that expansion necessarily worsens retention. The existing baseline churn remains the starting rate.
assumptions.author: olumi
